title: Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!
measurement_description: The paper measures the vulnerability of safety-aligned Large Language Models to fine-tuning attacks. As part of a broader safety evaluation on 11 harmfulness categories, it measures whether fine-tuned models can be 'jailbroken' to generate harmful, biased, or hateful content directed at religious groups, such as hate speech tweets or offensive jokes about religion.
religious_groups: Redacted religious groups (the authors replaced specific religious groups with '<religion group (redacted)>' to avoid propagating hate speech)
models_tested: GPT-4 (used as an automated safety judge)
findings: The study found that even highly aligned LLMs can be easily jailbroken through fine-tuning with a few adversarial examples or even benign datasets. When jailbroken, the models discard their safety guardrails and willingly fulfill harmful instructions, such as generating hate speech against religious groups, creating influence operations targeted at religious sects, and writing offensive jokes based on an individual's religion.
